1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.02.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.302/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, KOLAR, DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed in MVC No.302/2016 on 20-02-2018 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kolar, the petitioner is before this court in appeal.
2.
The brief facts are as below:

That on 9-2-2016 at around 3.00 PM., the petitioner Muniswamy @ Muniswamappa was proceeding towards his village from Mulbagal on his two wheeler bearing No.
KA- 07-W-9557 and when he reached Parashurama temple in Kolar, one APE goods auto bearing No. KA.07.7672 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against two wheelers bearing No. KA.08.J.6219 and to the two wheeler of petitioner bearing No. KA-07-W-9557.

Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained multiple and grievous injuries and immediately the petitioner was shifted to R.L. NC:
2023:KHC:20977 Jalappa hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment for a period of 2 months and even after discharge he continued to take treatment and has already spent `2.00 lakhs towards medical expenses.

The petitioner contended that the accident has taken place only due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Auto and even the Kolar Traffic Police authorities have registered a case as against the driver of APE goods auto bearing No. KA-07-7672 for the offence punishable U/s.
279, 337 and 338 of the IPC.

Respondent No.1 is the owner of the vehicle bearing No.
KA-07-7672 and respondent No.2 is the driver as well as the GPA holder of the vehicle bearing No. KA-07-7672 and therefore, they are liable to pay the compensation.

3. It was further contended by the petitioner that he is an agriculturist and Milk vendor by profession having monthly income of `40,000/ and now due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he is not in a position to do his day to day work and he has been put to monetary loss and hardship.
On issuance of the notice respondent Nos. 1 and 2, respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and respondent No.1 did not appear and he was placed exparte.

2
5. The 2nd respondent though has appeared through his counsel has not chosen to file objections to the main petition 6.
Before the Tribunal, the petitioner was examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and how much?
3. For what relief?
8.

The Tribunal answering point No.1 in the affirmative and point No.2 partly in the affirmative,
passed the following:
The petitioner is entitled for an award amount of Rs.1,71,125-00 (Rupees one lakh seventy one thousand one hundred twenty five only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The petition as against the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 is hereby dismissed.
Office to draw the award accordingly."
9. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this court in appeal.
10. The petitioner/appellant contended that the dismissal of the petition is erroneous and the liability on the part of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 has not be properly considered by the Tribunal.

It is contended that respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the NC: 2023:KHC:20977 driver and GPA holder of respondent No.1 and therefore, they should have been directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Apart from that, the quantum of compensation awarded was also assailed by him.
11. On issuance of notice, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The Tribunal records have been secured on admitting the appeal.

12. Heard the arguments by learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant submitted that when the chargesheet discloses that respondent No.2 was the driver of the goods auto, irrespective of whether the name of respondent No.1 finds place in the chargesheet, the Tribunal should have fastened the liability on respondent No.2.

It is pointed out that the Tribunal has lost sight of the fact that respondent No.2 was the tortfeaser and therefore, it could not have NC: 2023:KHC:20977 dismissed the petition against both the respondents.
He also points out that though the Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for an award amount of `1,75,125/-, it dismissed the petition against respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
There being no other respondents, the impugned order is strange and unsustainable.
Therefore, he contended that the judgment and award is bereft of any application of mind.
Further, he contends that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of loss of amenities in life and as such, the enhancement in the compensation amount may also be granted.
14. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that in the absence of the owner of the vehicle, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
He submits that owner of the vehicle is liable vicariously and therefore, it is essential that the name of the owner of the vehicle is to be proved by the petitioner.
A perusal of the Tribunal records would show that the FIR is produced at Ex.P1 and it clearly mentions that the driver of the goods Ape Auto was at fault.
Subsequently, the investigation was conducted by the Investigating Officer and chargesheet was lodged as per Ex.P2.
In Ex.P2 the name of respondent No.2-R Joseph Royal @ Sunil, has been shown to be the accused and the driver of the said goods auto.
Further, the chargesheet also discloses that the said goods auto was not having an insurance policy and therefore, he was prosecuted for the offence under Section 196 of MV Act also.
Therefore, it is evident that respondent No.2 was the driver of the said ape goods auto.
16. It is the basic principles of any tortfeasance that the primary liability is on the tortfeaser.
The owner of the such vehicle is liable on the principles of vicarious liability.
The role of the insurer comes into play on account of contractual liability.
In the case on hand, it is evident that the owner of the goods auto is not known.
Either the NC: 2023:KHC:20977 chargesheet, FIR or any other documents produced by the petitioner do not disclose that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the vehicle.
Nowhere, in any of the documents produced, the name of respondent No.1 is found to be the owner of the vehicle.
The chargesheet mentions that on 17.2.2016, the accused, who is respondent No.2 herein, had produced the said goods auto and it was seized by the investigating officer.
Therefore, it is evident that primarily, it was the respondent No.2 being the driver of the vehicle was liable as a tortfeaser.
17. There is absolutely no material is available on record to show that respondent No.1 was the owner of the auto.

The learned counsel appearing for appellant submits that the chargesheet papers indicate that the respondent No.2 was the GPA holder of owner and he had got released the said auto on behalf of the owner.
His submission before the Court is not supported by any document.
Such submission cannot be accepted in the absence of any documentary evidence including the GPA.

Therefore, the Muniswamy @ Muniswamappa vs H. Anandkumar on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175111297/
4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20977 impugned judgment and award so far as it relates to the dismissal of the petition as against respondent No.2 is not sustainable.
Such an order do not stand for any logical reason also.

It is apparent that the Tribunal without applying its mind to the basics of law of tort,
has proceeded to dismiss the petition against the respondent No.2.
18.

Coming to the quantum of the compensation, it is evident that the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of `1,71,125/- under different heads as below:
 Pain and suffering ` 25,000/-
Medical expenses ` 56,125/-
Food nourishment, conveyance and attendant ` 30,000/-
charges Loss of income during laid up period ` 60,000/-
However, it is evident that, The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities' in life.
There are more than two fractures - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20977 sustained by the petitioner.
The petitioner contends that he was aged about 46 years and was an agriculturist and milk vendor by profession.
Under these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of `40,000/- towards the loss of amenities in life.
Hence, there shall be an enhancement of compensation to the extent of `40,000/- with interest.
20. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal is modified by setting aside the same insofar as dismissal of petition against respondent No.2 and holding that the appellant is entitled for a sum of `40,000/- in addition to Rs.1,71,125/- that has been determined by the Tribunal along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit.
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20977 Muniswamy @ Muniswamappa vs H. Anandkumar on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175111297/
5
(iii) The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount along with accrued interest within six weeks from the date of this order before the Tribunal.
(iv) In the event of such deposit.
the entire enhanced amount is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
(v) The petition as against respondent No.1 stands dismissed.
